page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-4 is an x86_64 architecture server instance within the n1 family, featuring 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. It operates with dedicated CPU allocation at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz and utilizes a 45 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local NVMe SSD storage or integrated GPU hardware, requiring external block storage for persistent data.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the n1-highcpu-4 delivers entry-level performance across compute and memory subsystems. In stress-ng testing, the instance achieved a single-core score of 1125.48 and a multi-core score of 2941.66, both falling into the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth tests show 162.49 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 25.58 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Geekbench 6 results align with these findings, showing a single-core score of 926.0 and a multi-core score of 1979.0, placing the instance in the bottom 10% for raw processing capacity.

The primary tradeoff of the n1-highcpu-4 is its highly constrained memory capacity of 4.0 GB relative to its 4 vCPUs, which limits its utility for memory-intensive applications. While it offers a dedicated CPU allocation, the older Intel Xeon architecture results in lower performance per resource compared to newer instance generations. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance is positioned as a budget-friendly option for compute-centric workloads that do not demand high memory density or modern instruction sets. It is best suited for lightweight web serving, basic software compilation, simple text processing, and small-scale batch processing tasks.
